rationale: Tests classification of CVA into ischaemic vs haemorrhagic subtypes — foundational schema covered in the Classification block.
Tests the penumbra concept — the core pathophysiological rationale for the reperfusion time window.
Tests the critical role of last-known-well time in stroke history, which drives thrombolysis eligibility.
Tests discrimination of Broca's vs Wernicke's aphasia — a high-yield bedside localisation skill covered in the Speech and Language Disorders block.
Tests the first-line imaging choice in acute stroke and the rationale for CT-first — a known-trap item.
Tests the expanded aetiological workup in young stroke, specifically the relevance of thrombophilia and arterial dissection screening.
Tests the BP threshold for IV thrombolysis eligibility — the most clinically critical threshold in acute stroke management.
Tests the time window for mechanical thrombectomy, distinguishing the standard 6-hour window from the extended 24-hour selected window.
Tests the timing of early mobilisation in stroke rehabilitation — the most evidence-supported principle in post-stroke care.
Tests counselling on driving post-stroke — a specific and commonly required patient counselling item.
